newsitem.title: FRANCE: France agrees price cuts on Dassault Rafale plane.
newsitem.headline: France agrees price cuts on Dassault Rafale plane.

text.p: The French DGA arms procurement agency has reached agreement with Dassault Aviation on price cuts on the Rafale combat plane, a defence ministry spokesman said on Thursday.

The spokesman confirmed comments made by Defence Minister Charles Millon in an interview with newspaper Les Echos, which reported him as saying: "On the subject of price, the negotiations have ended, thanks to the efforts...of the industrial companies involved, notably Dassault Aviation."
The DGA had been asking for a 10 percent reduction prior to agreeing multi-year funding for an order of 48 Rafale jets.

"Dassault made the offers we were looking for on lowering the production cost of the Rafale. That allows us to make the proposals to relaunch this programme," the head of the Delegation Generale de l'Armement (DGA), Jean-Yves Helmer, was reported as saying in newspaper La Tribune.
The unit cost of a Rafale is estimated at between 300-350 million francs.
The DGA is looking for an overall 30 percent cut in prices on programme costs in the six-year period covered by the current defence budget law.
